applies_why: The judge text does not count any verse from a side's cited-in line as an unanswered witness; it instead reports that the relevant points were answered and calls the issue underdetermined.
quote: the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
why: Because the judge says the relevant points were answered and does not count any verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link, it obeys K-G4.
